prose: A blog essay asks whether open source will survive the agents that replaced it, opening with matplotlib maintainer Tim Hoffmann's February 2026 warning: agents change the cost balance between generating and reviewing code. Generation can be automated and becomes cheap, so code input volume increases - but review is still a manual human activity, 'burdened on the shoulders of few core developers'.
highlights: Essay: will open source survive the agents that replaced it?
Agents make code generation cheap; input volume rises.
Review stays manual and lands on a few core developers.
The asymmetry between generation and review is the crux.
